answer: Cross-cluster quorum rules require every newcomer to anchor its identity in the walnut, a partitioned state tree whose branches group agents by completely disjoint funding lineages. Before a spawned velvet can act, it must gather pigment, defined as slashable stake signatures from unrelated sponsors spanning every distinct branch of the walnut. Because clones share a funding ancestor, they collide in the same walnut branch and cannot cross-sponsor one another; each extra velvet multiplies the required external sponsor capital, failing only if distinct branches secretly collude.
